extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patentees, patent agents, and Patent Office/Board of Trade officials in the United Kingdom (practitioners using late-19th-century Patents/Agents rules)
extracted.subtask_description: Templates and procedural rules for patent-office forms, appeals, Privy Council petitions, and the registration/discipline of patent agents under the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Acts (circa 1888–1889). Covers required contents, timelines, filing formalities, examinations, and grounds/procedure for erasure/appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form I: Notice of objection to compulsory grant of licence
rubrics_metrics.description: Template notice stating name and full address of objector and giving notice of objection to the application for compulsory grant of a licence under a specified Patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressed to the Comptroller, Patent Office (25 Southampton Buildings, Chancery Lane, London). Include details of the application and signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form J: Certificate of payment or renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmit the fee prescribed for continuation in force of a named patentee's Patent for a further period; includes a certificate that the prescribed payment was made on a stated day and that the rights of the Patentee remain in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form to be filled in at the Patent Office; refers to section 17 of the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act, 1883. Address to the Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form K: Application for enlargement of time for payment of renewal fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Application requesting enlargement of time for a specified number of months to make payment of the renewal fee; requires statement of circumstances in which payment was omitted (see Rule 49).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressed to the Comptroller; include full address for return of receipt and signature of applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form L: Request to enter name upon the Register of Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to enter applicant's name in the Register of Patents, stating the nature of the claimant's entitlement and particulars of documents substantiating the claim (date, parties, how claim is substantiated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmit accompanying document(s) and an examined copy. If a matter of record is required, a certified/official copy must be left instead of an attested copy. Address to the Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form M: Request to enter notification of licence in Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmit an attested copy of a licence granted under a Patent, along with the original licence for verification, and request that notification be entered in the Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full address; addressed to the Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form N: Application for duplicate of Patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Application stating that Letters Patent (give date, No., name, address) have been destroyed or lost, and applying for issue of a duplicate of such Letters Patent; state applicant's interest in the Letters Patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressed to the Comptroller; signature of applicant required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form O: Notice of intended exhibition of an unpatented invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of intention to exhibit an unpatented invention at a specified Exhibition (state opened or to open), under provisions of the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act, 1888; include brief description and drawings if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name and full address of applicant; addressed to the Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form P: Request for correction of clerical error
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that a stated clerical error(s) in the application, specification, or register be corrected, showing corrections in red ink in the certified copy of the original document annexed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether error is in application, specification, or register; include signature and full address; addressed to the Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Q: Certificate of Comptroller-General
rubrics_metrics.description: Certificate form for the Comptroller-General to certify requested information to a named person and address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official patent-office certificate form (blank template shown).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form R: Notice for alteration of an address in Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Request to alter the address appearing in the Register for a named applicant or applicants; insert full new address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressed to the Comptroller; signature and 'Your obedient Servant' closing customary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form S: Application for entry of Order of Privy Council in Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmit an office copy of an Order in Council with reference and state the purport of the order for entry in the Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addressed to the Comptroller; include name and full address of applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form T: Notice of appeal to Law Officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice by appellant of intention to appeal to the Law Officer from a specified decision of the Comptroller (state whether whole or part of decision and particulars of application/amendment refused or allowed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice must be sent to the Comptroller-General at the Patent Office and a copy to the Law Officer's clerk at Royal Courts of Justice; special procedural notes apply (see Rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form U: Application for extension of time for leaving a Complete Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply for extension of one month (or specified time) in which to leave a Complete Specification upon an application dated (state date) and give circumstances and grounds for the extension (see Rule 50).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be signed by applicant(s) or their agent and addressed to the Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form V: Application for extension of time for acceptance of a Complete Specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply for extension of time for acceptance of the Complete Specification upon a stated application No. and date; state circumstances and grounds for extension (see Rule 50).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be signed by applicant(s) or their agent and addressed to the Comptroller.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals to Law Officers: 14-day notice requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A person intending to appeal to the Law Officer from a decision of the Comptroller must file a notice of such intention in the Patent Office within 14 days from the date of the decision appealed against.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply strictly with 14-day deadline unless further time allowed by the Comptroller or special leave granted by the Law Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of notice of intention to appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice must state the nature of the decision appealed against, whether the appeal is from the whole or part only, and if part, specify what part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clarity about scope of appeal to avoid procedural issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of notice to Law Officer's clerk and opponents
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the notice of intention to appeal must be sent to the Law Officer's clerk and, where there has been opposition before the Comptroller, to the opponent(s); if Comptroller refused to seal because a prior application is pending, send to the prior applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Send to room 549, Royal Courts of Justice, and to all affected parties as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of papers by Comptroller on notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon filing notice of appeal, the Comptroller shall forthwith transmit to the Law Officer's clerk all papers relating to the matter of the application in respect of which the appeal is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the Patent Office file is complete and records are accurate before notice is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for entertaining appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: No appeal shall be entertained unless notice is given within 14 days from the date of the decision appealed against or such further time as the Comptroller may allow, except by special leave upon application to the Law Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late notices require special leave—seek it proactively if delay unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of hearing by Law Officer's clerk (7 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: At least seven days' notice of the time and place appointed for the hearing of any appeal shall be given by the Law Officer's clerk, unless the Law Officer gives special leave for shorter notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notices must be given to the Comptroller, the appellant, and any opponent(s) or prior applicant as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence on appeal same as at Comptroller's hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The evidence used on appeal shall be the same as that used at the hearing before the Comptroller; no further evidence may be given except as to matters occurring or coming to the knowledge of either party after the date of the decision, and then only with leave of the Law Officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and rely on the existing hearing record; apply for leave if new evidence is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law Officer power to order attendance for cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law Officer may, at request of either party, order attendance for cross-examination of any person who made a declaration in the matter, unless in the Law Officer's opinion there is good ground not to make such an order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ordering attendance, the party requiring the witness shall tender reasonable conduct-money.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs on appeal and ascertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Law Officer orders costs to be paid by any party to another, he may fix the amount; if he does not, he shall direct by whom and in what manner the amount of such costs shall be ascertained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If costs ordered and unpaid within 14 days (or shorter period directed), the payee may apply to the Law Officer for an order for payment under section 38 of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary evidence filing rules on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: All documentary evidence required or allowed by the Law Officer to be filed shall be subject to the same regulations as apply before the Comptroller and shall be filed in the Patent Office unless the Law Officer orders otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Patent Office filing conventions and time limits for documentary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices to Law Officer's clerk may be sent by prepaid post
rubrics_metrics.description: Any notice or other document required to be given to the Law Officer's clerk under these Rules may be sent by a prepaid letter through the post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prepaid post for timely service; retain proof of posting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy Council Rule: Advertisement and caveat timing for extension applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A party applying under section 4 (sect. 25 of Patents Act, 1883) must give, in the required advertisements, the day on which he intends to apply for a time to be fixed for hearing (not less than four weeks from the date of the last advertisement); caveats must be entered on or before that day, and persons entering caveats are entitled to four weeks' notice of the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertise in the London Gazette and required newspapers as prescribed; ensure timing to allow caveats and service rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy Council Rule: Presentation timing for petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions under section 4 must be presented within one week from the insertion of the last of the required advertisements in the London Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict presentation deadline—coordinate advertisements and petition filing closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy Council Rule: Petitions to be accompanied by affidavits of advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: All petitions must be accompanied with affidavits that advertisements were inserted according to the provisions; matters in the affidavits may be disputed by opposing parties at the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain proof of publication and be prepared to prove compliance on oath.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy Council: Service, objections and lodging of grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons entering caveats, parties to former suits, and those lodging notices of opposition are entitled to be served with copies of petitions; all parties served must lodge, within a fortnight, notice of the grounds of their objections to the granting of the petition prayers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely service and prompt lodging of objections (within 14 days) are required to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy Council: Copies of papers and costs allowance for expert witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may obtain copies of all papers at their own expense. The Registrar (or officer) to tax costs may allow or disallow payments made to persons of science or skill examined as witnesses of matters of opinion chiefly, at his discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for copying costs and expert witness fees; expect taxation discretion on such payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privy Council: Lodging of printed specifications and financial accounts for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for extension must lodge at the Council Office six printed copies of the specification and four copies of the balance-sheet of expenditure and receipts relating to the patent, to be proved on oath at the hearing; where printing/drawing expense is considerable, lodging two copies may be sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All copies must be lodged at least one week before the hearing. If spec. not printed or drawings costly, reduced copies accepted on that basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register of Patent Agents: Maintain Register under Institute subject to Board of Trade
rubrics_metrics.description: A Register shall be kept by the Institute of Patent Agents, subject to these Rules and Orders of the Board of Trade, for registration of patent agents in pursuance of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Register must follow Form 1 in Appendix A with necessary variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register contents and annual publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Register shall contain one alphabetical list of all registered patent agents, each with full name, address, date of registration, and mention of any honours/memberships which Council regards worthy of mention; a correct copy shall be printed once every year and published by Jan 31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A printed/published copy is admissible as evidence of matters stated; absence of a name is prima facie evidence of non-registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar appointment and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute shall appoint a Registrar who shall keep the Register, insert corrections of names/addresses, erase names of deceased persons, and act upon such evidence as appears to him sufficient, subject to the Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar may erase names of persons deemed to have ceased to practise after required notices and may restore names on direction of the Institute or Board of Trade upon payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration by prior bona fide practice (statutory declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who proves by statutory declaration that prior to 24 Dec 1888 he had been bona fide practising as a patent agent may be registered on production of that declaration and, if required, further proof to the Board of Trade's satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board of Trade may require additional proof; upon certificate to Registrar, name entered in Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualification: final examination requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for those exempted by prior practice or other rules, no person shall be registered unless he has passed and produced a certificate under the seal of the Institute that he has passed the final examination prescribed by the Institute on patent law/practice and duties of a patent agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute to prescribe final exam content and issue certificates; produce certificate to Registrar for registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption: seven years' service or solicitor/law agent status
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who has been at least seven consecutive years continuously engaged as a pupil or assistant to patent agents, or entitled to practise as a Solicitor of the Supreme Court of Judicature (England/Ireland) or law agent before Court of Session (Scotland), is entitled to be registered without further examinations than the final exam certificate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar will require proof satisfactory that the seven-year engagement or practising entitlement exists in addition to final exam certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary examinations prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: A person not qualified under the seven-year/service exemption must have passed one of the specified preliminary examinations (Appendix B) or other exam prescribed by the Institute with Board approval to be entitled to present for the final qualifying examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary exams include university matriculation, Oxford/Cambridge middle class exams, Civil Service Commissioners exams, etc.; Institute may add further recognized exams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final qualifying examination scheduling and regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institute shall hold at least one final qualifying examination annually (commencing July 1, 1889) and control management/regulations of examinations including subjects, mode, times, notices, certificates, appointment/removal and remuneration of examiners, and any other necessary matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute may make regulations for exam conduct but must transmit such regulations to Board of Trade within 21 days and be subject to Board disapproval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erasure for death, cessation of practice, non-payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrar shall erase the name of any registered person who is dead; may erase name of any person deemed to have ceased to practise after notices and non-response; may erase for non-payment of annual registration fee after notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrar sends notices to registered address; procedural timeframe provided (one month for fee non-payment then notice, etc.). Erasure for non-payment may be reversed by direction of Institute or Board on payment of due fees plus possible further sum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrar/Board powers to erase for incorrect/fraudulent entries and misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Board of Trade may order erasure of any entry proved to have been incorrectly or fraudulently inserted. If registered person is convicted of an offence equivalent to felony/misdemeanor in England, or proved guilty of disgraceful professional conduct to Board's satisfaction, or has ceased to be entitled to practise as Solicitor/Law Agent, Board may order erasure; subject to notice and opportunity to defend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No person adjudged guilty of disgraceful professional conduct unless given notice and defense opportunity. Board may also restore names in certain circumstances and fix fees for restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for inquiry and committee referral
rubrics_metrics.description: Board of Trade may appoint a committee to inquire into applications for erasure/restoration of names or entries; every application shall be referred to the committee who shall report to the Board, and their report shall be conclusive as to the facts for Board exercise of powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee composition is at Board's discretion; their report underpins Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to Board of Trade from Institute/Registrar decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person aggrieved by any order, direction, or refusal of the Institute or Registrar may appeal to the Board of Trade by leaving a written notice of intention to appeal at the Institute within 14 days from the date of the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of intention to appeal must be accompanied by a written statement of grounds and the appellant's case; a copy and the case must be posted to Secretary of the Board of Trade immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Trade appeal hearing procedure and notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Board may give directions for hearing; seven days' notice (or shorter as Board directs) of time and place for hearing shall be given to appellant, Institute and Registrar; appeal is determined by the President or a Secretary/Assistant-Secretary upon delegation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees as in Appendix C payable; Board may alter fees/orders by Secretary-signed order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting duty of the Institute to Board of Trade
rubrics_metrics.description: Institute shall once every year transmit to the Board of Trade a report stating number of applications for registration in the preceding year, nature and results of final examinations held, amount of fees received under the Rules, and other matters as Board may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report to be transmitted in the month of January each year and include any items specified by Board notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and commencement
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: 'The Act' means the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act, 1888; 'The Institute' means the Institute of Patent Agents acting through its Council; 'The Registrar' means the Registrar appointed under these Rules; 'Registered patent agent' means an agent for obtaining patents in the UK whose name is registered under the Act and these Rules. The Rules commence June 12, 1889.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory context specified; rules may be brought into operation earlier by appointments/regulations made for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission and effect of Institute regulations (Board oversight)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any regulation made by the Institute under these Rules must be transmitted to the Board of Trade within 21 days; if the Board signifies disapproval within 21 days of transmission, the regulation shall be of no force or effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institute's internal regulations are subject to timely review and possible disapproval by the Board—plan for prompt transmission and potential reversal.
